headline: RADISSON MINING HITS GOLD AT 1,720M VERTICAL DEPTH AT O'BRIEN — 5 ZONES INTERSECTED IN DEEPEST HOLE YET AS 8-RIG CAMPAIGN EXTENDS ABITIBI DISCOVERY
source_name: ACN Newswire — Radisson Mining Resources Inc. (TSXV: RDS)
snippet: Radisson Mining Resources Inc. (TSXV: RDS) released drill results on June 22, 2026 confirming gold mineralisation at 1,720 metres vertical depth at the O'Brien Gold Project's 'O'Brien Mine East' zone — the deepest intersection in the project's history — with hole OB-26-378W3 cutting five separate gold-bearing zones at that depth and extending the known footprint of the Abitibi Greenstone Belt deposit in multiple directions simultaneously. The 140,000-metre drill program has eight rigs active across the property, following the March 2026 updated mineral resource estimate. For retail investors in TSXV-listed Québec gold explorers, a 1,720-metre vertical intercept on an 8-rig program confirms the system has depth potential well beyond the current resource envelope — the key driver of resource growth that distinguishes a single-discovery junior from a district-scale asset.

headline: ZACATECAS SILVER ESPERANZA GOLD RESOURCE UP 21% TO 1.15 MOZ AUÉQ — 45.4MT AT 0.79 G/T HEAP-LEACH GRADE ABOVE GLOBAL INDUSTRY AVERAGE IN MORELOS, MEXICO
snippet: Zacatecas Silver Corp. (TSXV: ZAC) released an updated mineral resource estimate on June 22, 2026 for its Esperanza Gold Project in Morelos State, Mexico — prepared by P&E Mining Consultants Inc. and effective April 6, 2026 — showing a 21% increase in the heap-leach constrained resource to 1.15 million ounces AuEq from 45.4 million tonnes at 0.79 g/t AuEq, above the global average grade for heap-leach deposits. Highest-grade material is concentrated at surface, the geometry most favourable for low-strip heap-leach processing economics. For retail investors evaluating TSXV-listed Mexican gold developers, a 21% resource increase at above-average heap-leach grades in a surface-weighted deposit defines the specific upgrade trajectory — larger tonnes, better grade, near-surface — that drives the capital markets re-rating from explorer to near-term developer.

headline: NOVA MINERALS REDOMICILES TO US, LISTS ON NYSE AMERICAN AS NVA — US$43.4M DOD TITLE III DEFENSE PRODUCTION ACT FUNDING BACKS ALASKA ANTIMONY PROJECT
source_name: GlobeNewswire / Manila Times — Nova Minerals (NYSE American / ASX: NVA)
snippet: Nova Minerals (NYSE American: NVA) announced on June 22, 2026 that its redomicile from Australia to the United States is complete and effective June 16 — with shares trading on NYSE American from June 17 — accompanied by a project update confirming US$43.4 million in US Department of Defense funding under Defense Production Act Title III, delivered via its subsidiary Alaska Range Resources (85% interest in the Estelle Project). Military-grade antimony trisulfide samples are nearing completion, a 10,000-metre drill program is set to begin, and pilot-scale antimony production is targeted for late 2026 to early 2027, with over A$89.4 million in total funding available as of the March 2026 quarter. For retail investors tracking critical mineral projects with US government backing, the combination of DoD Title III funding, NYSE American listing, and domestic US redomicile positions Nova Minerals directly in the supply chain infrastructure the Defense Production Act was designed to create — with antimony's role in military ordnance, flame retardants, and energy storage now explicitly funded at the federal programme level.

headline: CAPSTONE COPPER LOCKS IN 3-YEAR LABOUR PEACE AT MANTOS BLANCOS — BOTH UNIONS RATIFY AHEAD OF SECTION 232 TARIFF IMPLEMENTATION PERIOD
snippet: Capstone Copper Corp. (TSX: CS) announced on June 21, 2026 that both unions at the Mantos Blancos copper mine in Chile's Antofagasta region have ratified three-year collective bargaining agreements, locking in labour peace through 2029 across a workforce of approximately 1,106 direct employees (92% local) and 2,928 total personnel including contractors. The agreements remove strike risk at one of Capstone's flagship Chilean operations at a moment when Section 232 copper tariff implementation uncertainty is making uninterrupted copper supply from allied-jurisdiction producers a premium-grade asset for offtake counterparties. For retail investors holding TSX-listed mid-tier copper producers, a three-year CBA at a major Chilean operation eliminates the category of operational disruption most likely to trigger guidance cuts during a period when copper's tariff narrative is already compressing peer multiples.
